1	# Requirements
     2	
     3	Paths are relative to the `emr-sync-driver` repository root unless prefixed
     4	`vault/` (HDP repository, hub feedback). Foundations and security posture
     5	are user-ratified in `vault/research/computer-use-emr-sync/` and are
     6	constraints here, not open questions.
     7	
     8	## Functional
     9	
    10	- FR-001: WHEN the bootstrap phase executes, the system SHALL exist as a
    11	  public GitHub repository `peterkc/emr-sync-driver` (MIT license, uv
    12	  project, Python >=3.13, CI running lint + type check + tests) — creation
    13	  itself gated on main-session user sign-off (irreversible op).
    14	- FR-002: WHEN `docker compose up` runs on the development machine (arm64),
    15	  the sandbox SHALL provide a version-pinned OpenEMR instance and a
    16	  Postgres instance (DBOS system database), seeded with synthetic patients
    17	  only.
    18	- FR-003: WHEN a demo sync job runs against the sandbox, the driver SHALL
    19	  log in programmatically (credentials sourced from environment/secret
    20	  store, never present in any LLM-visible surface), navigate to a target
    21	  synthetic patient, read a named field, write a named field, and verify
    22	  the write by re-reading the field.
    23	- FR-004: every job step SHALL execute as a DBOS step with its completion
    24	  checkpointed in Postgres; WHEN the driver process dies mid-job (including
    25	  SIGKILL), a resume SHALL complete the job from the last completed step
    26	  WITHOUT re-applying completed writes (idempotency keys on write steps).
    27	- FR-005: every browser action SHALL append a structured audit event
    28	  (timestamp, job id, step id, action, locator, outcome, failure class if
    29	  any) to an append-only store; the CLI SHALL replay a job's audit log
    30	  action-by-action in order.
    31	- FR-006: the driver SHALL expose the same job operations through both
    32	  surfaces: a typed CLI (run / resume / status / audit replay) and a thin
    33	  FastAPI service (submit job, get status, resume) publishing an OpenAPI
    34	  schema — the HTTP shape the future `hh-emr-sync` adapter integrates
    35	  against.
    36	- FR-007: WHEN a step fails, the driver SHALL classify the failure as one
    37	  of `dead-session | latency | selector-drift | unknown` BEFORE any retry
    38	  decision, and the classification SHALL land in the audit event.
    39	- FR-008: the browser context SHALL enforce a default-deny egress allowlist
    40	  (sandbox hosts only) via request routing as defense-in-depth, with
    41	  blocked requests logged; authoritative network-layer enforcement is
    42	  documented for production topologies (not implemented in the tracer).
    43	- FR-009: session artifacts (Playwright storage_state) SHALL be treated as
    44	  bearer credentials: stored outside the repository tree with file mode
    45	  0600, and absent from audit events, checkpoints, logs, and traces.
    46	- FR-010: WHEN the deterministic thread is proven end-to-end (FR-003/004
    47	  acceptance passed), a gated fallback phase SHALL evaluate Stagehand BYOB
    48	  as the selector-drift recovery layer behind a driver-owned seam
    49	  interface; the deterministic path SHALL make zero LLM calls, and
    50	  evaluation findings (including the open agent-cache replay question)
    51	  SHALL be recorded to the research hub.
    52	
    53	## Non-functional
    54	
    55	- NFR-001: tracer-bullet quality (kept code): every code phase lands with
    56	  `ruff check` clean, `mypy src/` clean, and `pytest` green in CI — no
    57	  placeholder bodies on the executed path, no skipped quality gates.
    58	- NFR-002 (negative-space): WHEN given invalid input at a trust boundary
    59	  (CLI args, env/config, API request bodies, selector-map files), the
    60	  system SHALL fail fast with a typed error — never crash, corrupt job
    61	  state, or write to the EMR on bad input.
    62	- NFR-003: synthetic-data-only scope: the egress allowlist and target
    63	  configuration SHALL admit only the local sandbox; no PHI exists anywhere
    64	  in the system, its logs, or its repository.
    65	- NFR-004: public-reader hygiene: repository and hub content SHALL carry
    66	  zero application-context leaks — verified before merge.
    67	
    68	## Acceptance criteria
    69	
    70	- AC-001: `gh repo view peterkc/emr-sync-driver --json visibility,licenseInfo`
    71	  reports PUBLIC + MIT; a fresh clone runs `uv run pytest` green; CI is
    72	  green on default branch. (FR-001)
    73	- AC-002: `docker compose up -d` then an HTTP probe returns the OpenEMR
    74	  login page; the compose file pins an explicit OpenEMR version tag; a
    75	  seeded synthetic patient is retrievable. (FR-002)
    76	- AC-003: `uv run emr-sync run field-roundtrip --patient <synthetic-id>`
    77	  exits 0; the job's final audit event records read-after-write
    78	  verification success. (FR-003)
    79	- AC-004: an integration test SIGKILLs the driver mid-job, then
    80	  `uv run emr-sync resume <job-id>` completes the job; the target field
    81	  holds the expected value exactly once and the audit log shows no
    82	  duplicate write application. (FR-004)
    83	- AC-005: `uv run emr-sync audit replay <job-id>` prints every action of
    84	  the job in order; the replayed action count equals the recorded step
    85	  actions. (FR-005)
    86	- AC-006: `POST /jobs` accepts a job, `GET /jobs/{id}` reports status
    87	  transitions, `POST /jobs/{id}/resume` resumes; `/openapi.json` serves the
    88	  schema. (FR-006)
    89	- AC-007: an induced selector miss is classified `selector-drift` and an
    90	  induced logout is classified `dead-session`, asserted on audit events.
    91	  (FR-007)
    92	- AC-008: a test request to a non-allowlisted host is blocked and a blocked

    94	- AC-009: a test asserts the storage_state file lives outside the repo tree

   100	- AC-011: with fallback disabled, a full job's audit log contains zero LLM
   101	  calls; with fallback enabled, an induced drift either recovers via the
   102	  seam or halts cleanly with classification — and the hub records the
   103	  Stagehand evaluation findings. (FR-010)
   104	- AC-012 (negative-space): for each trust boundary (CLI args, env/config,
   105	  API bodies, selector-map files), a test feeds malformed input and asserts
   106	  a typed error / non-zero exit, not a crash or an EMR write. (NFR-002)
   107	- AC-013: before merge, a hygiene grep over the full driver repository
   108	  content and the hub-feedback diff returns zero application-context hits

   110	  phase records the clean grep as gate evidence. (NFR-004)

1	# Design
     2	
     3	## Architecture
     4	
     5	The driver is the production skeleton of a browser-level EMR sync transport,
     6	built as the thinnest end-to-end thread that exercises every load-bearing
     7	joint: durable job orchestration, deterministic browser control, audit,
     8	failure classification, and the two integration surfaces (CLI, thin API).
     9	Extraction quality and OASIS modeling are explicitly not this system's
    10	concern — the infrastructure is.
    11	
    12	```
    13	  CLI (typer)            thin API (FastAPI)
    14	      |                        |
    15	      +----------+------------+
    16	                 v
    17	        DBOS workflow (field-roundtrip job)
    18	        each step checkpointed in Postgres
    19	        write steps carry idempotency keys
    20	                 |
    21	                 v
    22	        browser session (Playwright, Chromium)
    23	        programmatic login -> storage_state custody
    24	        egress: default-deny route() allowlist
    25	                 |                          |
    26	                 v                          v
    27	        selector map (versioned)      audit store (append-only)
    28	        miss -> failures.classify()   every action, replayable
    29	        drift -> fallback seam
    30	        (Stagehand BYOB, gated phase)
    31	                 |
    32	                 v
    33	        OpenEMR sandbox (docker-compose, pinned, synthetic-only)
    34	```
    35	
    36	Job lifecycle: a job submitted via CLI or API becomes a DBOS workflow; each
    37	browser interaction is a step whose completion is checkpointed. A killed
    38	driver resumes from the last completed step — completed writes are not
    39	re-applied because write steps consult their idempotency key before acting.
    40	Every action (including blocked egress and failures) appends an audit
    41	event; replay is a read of that stream in order. Failure classification
    42	runs before any retry decision so the taxonomy data is captured even when
    43	recovery succeeds.
    44	
    45	The fallback seam is a driver-owned Protocol: the deterministic path never
    46	imports or calls it (zero LLM calls, asserted by AC-011); the gated
    47	fallback-eval phase provides a Stagehand BYOB implementation behind it and
    48	measures recovery behavior plus the open agent-cache replay question.
    49	
    50	## Execution note (cross-repo)
    51	
    52	This spec lives in the HDP vault but its code phases execute in a clone of
    53	`emr-sync-driver`. Evidence and phase state record here
    54	(`vault/specs/emr-driver-tracer/`); the hub-feedback phase is the only one
    55	that edits HDP files (the research hub, via the vault worktree). Repo
    56	creation in the bootstrap phase is an irreversible op: main-session user
    57	sign-off, never delegated.
    58	
    59	## File manifest
    60	
    61	Single SoT is `tasks.yaml` `manifest:` (file -> new|modified -> purpose).
    62	Manifest paths are emr-sync-driver-relative except `vault/`-prefixed
    63	entries (HDP). For interface contracts (CLI signatures, data models, golden
    64	example, AC-mapped test manifest, behavior x backend matrix) see
    65	`reference/`.
    66	
    67	## Decisions
    68	
    69	Foundational decisions are NOT re-made here — they are user-ratified in the
    70	research hub's decision log (`vault/research/computer-use-emr-sync/state.yaml`,
    71	6 entries): DOM-first/vision-assist control loop, self-hosted pinned OpenEMR
    72	sandbox, structural security posture, taxonomy-from-spike-runs, Playwright +
    73	DBOS foundations, deployment topology. Duplicating them as ADRs would create
    74	mirror drift; this section records only spec-local decisions:
    75	
    76	- **Standalone driver, converge later** (interview Dim 3): the tracer
    77	  depends on no HDP package — HDP primitives are pre-trim shells and #11 is
    78	  in flight. The thin API is the convergence seam: its job operations are
    79	  the HTTP shape the `hh-emr-sync` adapter will consume, and the driver's
    80	  audit/checkpoint interfaces inform HDP's primitives from real usage.
    81	- **Fallback gated behind deterministic E2E** (interview Dim 2): the
    82	  deterministic skeleton must pass AC-003/AC-004 before any LLM-assist code
    83	  lands. Couples one unknown per phase; preserves the zero-LLM property of
    84	  the primary path as a tested invariant rather than a hope.
    85	- **Sessions are cattle** (from research, operationalized here):
    86	  storage_state is a bearer credential — custody rules in FR-009; on
    87	  session death the driver re-authenticates rather than persisting
    88	  long-lived session stores.
    89	- **Audit store is driver-local Postgres, not HDP's audit package**:
    90	  consequence of standalone-first. The event shape (models.py AuditEvent)
    91	  is written so a later HDP adapter can map it 1:1 into platform audit
    92	  primitives.
    93	
    94	## Risks
    95	
    96	- DBOS + Playwright interaction is unproven in this combination (async
    97	  Playwright inside DBOS steps; step granularity vs browser session
    98	  affinity). The tracer phase exists to surface exactly this class of
    99	  unknown early — if step-per-action is too chatty, the fallback design is
   100	  step-per-page-interaction with action-level audit retained.
   101	- OpenEMR compose specifics (ports, default creds, seeding) are known
   102	  unknowns resolved at bootstrap (hub open questions); they affect setup
   103	  cost, not architecture.
   104	- `connect_over_cdp` reattach topology (browser survives driver death) is
   105	  documented lower-fidelity; the tracer's SIGKILL test targets driver-process
   106	  death with browser relaunch + storage_state re-injection, which is the
   107	  supported path. Browser-process survival is an optimization, not a
   108	  requirement.

     8	# emr-driver-tracer
     9	
    10	## Summary
    11	
    12	Build the tracer bullet for the computer-use EMR sync transport (GH #18,
    13	parent #14): a new public repository `emr-sync-driver` containing the
    14	thinnest production-quality thread — programmatic login to a self-hosted
    15	synthetic OpenEMR, read one field, write one field, verify by re-reading —
    16	with every step DBOS-checkpointed, every action audited and replayable,
    17	failures classified before retry, and the same job operations exposed via
    18	CLI and a thin FastAPI surface. Deliberate failure injection (SIGKILL
    19	mid-job, induced selector miss, killed session) seeds the research hub's
    20	failure taxonomy with >=3 observed rows. A gated final code phase evaluates
    21	Stagehand BYOB as the drift-recovery fallback; the deterministic path makes
    22	zero LLM calls by tested invariant. Kept code, no shortcuts: foundations
    23	are the user-ratified research decisions, and the custom surface (selector
    24	maps, audit, classification, adapter-shaped API) is the part with research
    25	value.
    26	
    27	## Risks & Unknowns
    28	
    29	- DBOS step granularity vs Playwright session affinity — unproven
    30	  combination; surfaced deliberately by the tracer phase (design.md §
    31	  Risks).
    32	- OpenEMR compose ports/credentials/seeding — known unknowns resolved at
    33	  bootstrap (carried from hub open questions).
    34	- Stagehand Python agent-cache replay path — UNVERIFIED in research;
    35	  answered empirically in the fallback-eval phase.
    36	- Dim 1 "thin API" interpretation (job submit/status/resume, no UI) was
    37	  orchestrator-inferred and challenger-validated; if the adapter contract
    38	  needs a different surface, it shows up at #11 integration, not here.

    13	audit_app = typer.Typer(name="audit", no_args_is_help=True)

    21	
    22	## Situation

    24	Many EMR systems serving home health expose weak or no integration APIs.

    26	presuming an API that many target systems lack (GH #14). OpenEMR is already

    30	## Complication
    31	
    32	Browser-level automation (DOM-driven, vision-assisted) is a credible
    33	additional transport for API-poor targets, but credentialed browser sessions
    34	against a medical-records UI carry a threat model that HTTP clients do not:
    35	prompt injection from rendered content, credential exposure, and a long tail
    36	of workflow failure modes (session death, selector drift, latency cliffs,
    37	partial write-back). The driver must be credible *infrastructure*, not a demo.
    38	
    39	## Question
    40	
    41	What does a browser-level EMR sync transport need to be credible
    42	infrastructure: how are credentialed sessions secured, which sandbox grounds
    43	the work, and how do long-running browser workflows against EMR UIs actually
    44	fail?
    45	
    46	## Approach
    47	
    48	Two gather waves on 2026-06-11 (see `state.yaml` for the plan). Wave one:
    49	prior vault context, the OpenEMR public demo page, OpenEMR Docker self-hosting
    50	docs, and Anthropic's computer-use security/limitations documentation. Wave
    51	two (build-vs-adopt): framework evaluations of the Stagehand Python SDK,
    52	browser-use, Skyvern, and Playwright, plus cloud deployment options — each
    53	evaluated against the wave-one decisions rather than in the abstract. The
    54	failure taxonomy below is a seed structure — its rows accrue from tracer-spike
    55	runs in the driver repository, each observed class feeding retry/idempotency/
    56	observability design.
    57	
    58	## Findings
    59	
    60	### Security posture
    61	
    62	Grounded in the vendor's own guidance for computer-use agents
    63	[ai-found: raw/04]:
    64	
    65	1. **Synthetic data only.** The sandbox holds zero real patient data, ever.
    66	   This is scope, not mitigation — there is no failure mode in which PHI is
    67	   exposed because no PHI exists in the loop.
    68	2. **Container isolation, minimal privileges.** The driver and the browser it
    69	   controls run in a dedicated container/VM ("dedicated virtual machine or
    70	   container with minimal privileges" — raw/04). The Anthropic reference
    71	   implementation itself is Docker-contained.
    72	3. **Network allowlist.** The browser environment can reach the sandbox EMR
    73	   and nothing else ("limiting internet access to an allowlist of domains" —
    74	   raw/04). An injected instruction cannot exfiltrate to a host it cannot
    75	   resolve.
    76	4. **Credentials outside the model loop.** DOM-first automation performs
    77	   login programmatically (selectors + secret store), so credentials never
    78	   enter a prompt. The vendor path of last resort — credentials in prompt XML
    79	   tags — is documented to increase prompt-injection blast radius (raw/04);
    80	   the DOM-first default avoids it structurally.
    81	5. **Session/audit boundary.** Every driver action that mutates EMR state is
    82	   logged as an auditable event; write-back operations carry idempotency keys
    83	   so a replay after partial failure cannot double-apply. This is where the
    84	   driver meets HDP's audit/provenance primitives.
    85	6. **HITL gates on consequential writes.** Human confirmation before
    86	   meaningful real-world consequences (raw/04) aligns with HDP's existing
    87	   confidence-gated HITL design — the transport inherits the platform's
    88	   review checkpoint rather than inventing its own.
    89	7. **Prompt-injection stance.** Rendered EMR content is untrusted input.
    90	   Defense in depth: DOM-first control (the model is not steering from
    91	   screenshots in the default path), Anthropic's screenshot classifiers when
    92	   vision assist is active, allowlisted egress, and HITL gates — the docs are
    93	   explicit that precautions remain necessary even with the classifier layer
    94	   (raw/04).
    95	
    96	### Sandbox selection — self-hosted OpenEMR (decision)
    97	
    98	**Decision: self-hosted OpenEMR via the official Docker production compose,
    99	version-pinned.** [ai-found: raw/02, raw/03]
   100	
   101	| Criterion | Public demo (`demo.openemr.io`) | Self-hosted Docker |
   102	| --- | --- | --- |
   103	| State persistence | Wiped daily at 8:00 UTC | We control reset timing |
   104	| Isolation | Shared with other visitors | Single-tenant |
   105	| Authorization for automated traffic | No AUP stated either way | Our infrastructure |
   106	| Version stability | Tracks upstream | Pinned (e.g. `7.0.3`) |
   107	| Synthetic patients | Two portal patients guaranteed | Seeded deliberately |
   108	| Setup cost | Zero | `docker compose up`, ~5-10 min, arm64-capable |
   109	
   110	The daily wipe alone disqualifies the public demo for failure-taxonomy work —
   111	multi-day observation of session death and drift requires state we own. The
   112	demo remains useful for quick manual UI recon. Gap to resolve at spike time:
   113	default ports/credentials and synthetic-data loading live in the Docker Hub
   114	page/compose files, not DOCKER_README.md (raw/03).
   115	
   116	### DOM-first, vision-assist (decision)
   117	
   118	**Decision: DOM-driven automation is the primary control loop; vision is
   119	assist and fallback.** The vendor's own limitation list argues for this
   120	[ai-found: raw/04]: latency "too slow compared to regular human-directed
   121	computer actions," coordinate hallucination in vision-driven clicking,
   122	scrolling unreliability, and degraded reliability against niche applications
   123	— EMR UIs being exactly that. DOM selectors are deterministic, fast, cheap,
   124	and auditable (a selector either matched or it didn't; a logged action replay
   125	is exact). Vision assist earns its place where the DOM fails: canvas-rendered
   126	or legacy widgets, selector-drift recovery (visually re-locating a control
   127	whose selector broke), and CAPTCHAs-class anomalies that should halt for human
   128	review anyway.
   129	
   130	### Failure taxonomy (seed)
   131	
   132	Classes named in #18; rows accrue from spike runs in the driver repo. Each
   133	observed failure gets: detection signal, blast radius, hardening
   134	recommendation.
   135	
   136	| Class | What it looks like | Hardening direction (hypothesis) |
   137	| --- | --- | --- |
   138	| Session death | Auth timeout/logout mid-workflow | Checkpointed orchestration; re-auth + resume from last checkpoint |
   139	| Selector drift | EMR update changes DOM; selectors stop matching | Versioned selector maps; vision-assisted re-location; drift alarms |
   140	| Latency cliffs | Page loads stall; waits time out unpredictably | Adaptive timeouts; circuit breakers; observability on wait distributions |
   141	| Partial write-back | Multi-field form submit interrupted midway | Idempotency keys; read-after-write verification; transactional batching where the UI allows |
   142	
   143	The infrastructure interest is in this column structure — retries,
   144	idempotent write-back, checkpointed orchestration, observability — more than
   145	in any single extraction's accuracy.
   146	
   147	### Build-vs-adopt: framework evaluation (decision, proposed)
   148	
   149	**Decision: build the driver on Playwright (deterministic loop) + DBOS
   150	(durable checkpoint/resume); evaluate Stagehand's BYOB pattern for the
   151	LLM-fallback layer during the spike; borrow browser-use's DOM serialization
   152	and Skyvern's failure semantics as reference architecture, not dependencies.**
   153	[ai-found: raw/05, raw/06, raw/07; durable execution raw/08]
   154	
   155	The 2026 production consensus independently converged on the hub's wave-one
   156	control-loop decision: deterministic DOM code primary, LLM engaged only where
   157	the page is unpredictable. Evaluated against that decision:
   158	
   159	| Candidate | License | Verdict | Why |
   160	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
   161	| Playwright (Python) | Apache-2.0 | **Adopt** — deterministic engine | Auto-waiting, storage_state login reuse, per-action traces, CDP reconnect (browser survives driver restart); no disqualifiers. Gap list (audit log, re-auth loop, step retry, egress enforcement) is the driver's actual product surface |
   162	| DBOS Transact | MIT | **Adopt** — checkpoint/resume layer | Embedded Python library, Postgres-backed (matches stack); crash-resume from last completed step; collapses workflow engine + queue + idempotency ledger into one component |
   163	| Stagehand Python SDK | MIT (SDK + server) | **Evaluate in spike** — fallback layer | BYOB maps exactly onto DOM-first/LLM-fallback (own Playwright page passes into `observe/act/extract`); fully self-hostable via embedded open-source server. Frictions: Node server sidecar, Python SDK lacks act-level caching/self-heal the TS original has |
   164	| browser-use | MIT (core) | **Reference / possible component** | Indexed-element DOM serializer is the best off-the-shelf page representation for drift recovery and is callable standalone; but pre-1.0 with two foundation swaps in 18 months, and its deterministic-replay sister project (workflow-use) is early-stage and AGPL |
   165	| Skyvern | AGPL-3.0 | **Reference architecture only** | LLM-per-step control loop inverts the ratified decision; AGPL bars a hard dependency in an MIT driver repo. Worth reading: stable-ID element tree + annotated-screenshot grounding, mutation-observer drift detection, workflow failure semantics (`continue_on_failure`, error-code mapping, human-pause blocks) |
   166	
   167	What remains in-house — and is the differentiating surface, not incidental
   168	glue: versioned selector maps, EMR workflow definitions, read-after-write
   169	verification, the structured PHI-minimal audit log, failure classification
   170	(one `TimeoutError` → dead-session vs latency vs drift), and the
   171	`hh-emr-sync` adapter contract. Notably, no evaluated framework ships durable
   172	checkpoint/resume for long-running jobs — confirming the seam the wave-one
   173	contract analysis identified.
   174	
   175	### Cloud deployment (decision, proposed)
   176	
   177	**Decision: spike runs local/single-VM (synthetic data — anywhere works);
   178	the production-shaped reference topology is self-hosted workers on a
   179	BAA-covered cloud, with managed browser infrastructure recorded as a
   180	credible alternative.** [ai-found: raw/08]
   181	
   182	Self-hosted shape: container workers (ECS Fargate-class — no runtime limits,
   183	~2 GB per browser task) pulling jobs from the Postgres-backed queue;
   184	checkpoint store and outbox in the same Postgres; secrets manager for EMR
   185	credentials; VPC egress allowlist enforced at the network layer (the
   186	wave-one posture's structural control, in cloud terms); LLM-assist calls
   187	routed through a BAA-covered model platform so even fallback screenshots
   188	stay inside one compliance boundary. One practical constraint shapes the
   189	topology: EMR and payer portals frequently allowlist source IPs, so egress
   190	must present a static IP (NAT/pinned proxy) — native to a VPC, awkward for
   191	rotating managed fleets.
   192	
   193	Managed alternative: Browserbase (the infrastructure behind Stagehand)
   194	documents SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA BAAs on request, a zero-data-retention mode,
   195	and per-session dedicated VMs — so the managed path is compliance-viable,
   196	trading vendor dependency for isolation engineering not built in-house. The
   197	spike costs nothing to keep portable across both: the driver talks to a CDP
   198	endpoint either way.
   199	
   200	## Synthesis
   201	
   202	A credible browser-level EMR sync transport is **a hardened, audited,
   203	DOM-first driver running against owned, synthetic-only infrastructure** — not
   204	a vision-loop agent pointed at a shared demo. The security posture is mostly
   205	structural (isolation, allowlist, credentials outside the model loop,
   206	synthetic-only scope) rather than behavioral, which is what makes it
   207	defensible. The sandbox decision (self-hosted, pinned OpenEMR) follows from
   208	needing multi-day failure state; the DOM-first decision follows from the
   209	vendor's own limitation list. What remains genuinely open — how these
   210	workflows fail in practice — is empirical, and the taxonomy table is the
   211	instrument for capturing it.
   212	
   213	Adapter-contract implications for the `hh-emr-sync` seam (#11): the contract
   214	must accommodate idempotency keys, checkpoint/resume semantics, and
   215	asynchronous completion — an HTTP adapter satisfies these trivially; an
   216	automation adapter requires them. If the seam bakes in synchronous
   217	request/response, the automation transport will not slot in.
   218	
   219	The build-vs-adopt pass narrows what the driver repository actually is:
   220	foundations are adoptable (Playwright for the deterministic loop, DBOS for
   221	durability), so the repository's own code concentrates on the domain layer —
   222	selector maps, workflow definitions, audit, failure classification, and the
   223	adapter contract. That is the right shape for a tracer-bullet project: the
   224	custom code is exactly the part with research value.
   225	
   226	## Open questions
   227	
   228	- Driver repository: name and visibility (pending owner decision); hub links
   229	  out once created.
   230	- OpenEMR synthetic-patient seeding: best mechanism (built-in demo data vs
   231	  Synthea import) — resolve at spike time.
   232	- Default ports/credentials for the production compose — Docker Hub page.
   233	- Which OASIS-relevant OpenEMR workflows make the first tracer target (visit
   234	  documentation? assessment forms?).
   235	- Stagehand Python: does the agent-level cache entry have a server-side
   236	  replay-submission path, or is replay fully client-built? (raw/05 flags
   237	  UNVERIFIED) — measure during the spike's fallback evaluation.
   238	
   239	## Next actions
   240	
   241	- Create the driver repository (Playwright + DBOS scaffold per the
   242	  build-vs-adopt decision); first tracer run against self-hosted OpenEMR.
   243	- Begin populating taxonomy rows from observed failures (one hardening
   244	  recommendation per observed class — #18 exit condition).
   245	- Feed adapter-contract implications into the #11 trim spec's emr-sync seam.
   246	
   247	## Cross-references
   248	
   249	- `state.yaml` — structured state for AI re-load
   250	- `raw/` — per-source captures (01 vault context, 02 demo page, 03 Docker
   251	  docs, 04 Anthropic security, 05 Stagehand Python, 06 browser-use + Skyvern,
   252	  07 Playwright, 08 cloud deployment)

    22

     2	
     3	## Architecture
     4	
     5	The driver is the production skeleton of a browser-level EMR sync transport,
     6	built as the thinnest end-to-end thread that exercises every load-bearing
     7	joint: durable job orchestration, deterministic browser control, audit,
     8	failure classification, and the two integration surfaces (CLI, thin API).
     9	Extraction quality and OASIS modeling are explicitly not this system's
    10	concern — the infrastructure is.
    11	
    12	```
    13	  CLI (typer)            thin API (FastAPI)
    14	      |                        |
    15	      +----------+------------+
    16	                 v
    17	        DBOS workflow (field-roundtrip job)
    18	        each step checkpointed in Postgres
    19	        write steps carry idempotency keys
    20	                 |
    21	                 v
    22	        browser session (Playwright, Chromium)
    23	        programmatic login -> storage_state custody
    24	        egress: default-deny route() allowlist
    25	                 |                          |
    26	                 v                          v
    27	        selector map (versioned)      audit store (append-only)
    28	        miss -> failures.classify()   every action, replayable
    29	        drift -> fallback seam
    30	        (Stagehand BYOB, gated phase)
    31	                 |
    32	                 v
    33	        OpenEMR sandbox (docker-compose, pinned, synthetic-only)
    34	```
    35	
    36	Job lifecycle: a job submitted via CLI or API becomes a DBOS workflow; each
    37	browser interaction is a step whose completion is checkpointed. A killed
    38	driver resumes from the last completed step — completed writes are not
    39	re-applied because write steps consult their idempotency key before acting.
    40	Every action (including blocked egress and failures) appends an audit
    41	event; replay is a read of that stream in order. Failure classification
    42	runs before any retry decision so the taxonomy data is captured even when
    43	recovery succeeds.
    44	
    45	The fallback seam is a driver-owned Protocol: the deterministic path never
    46	imports or calls it (zero LLM calls, asserted by AC-011); the gated
    47	fallback-eval phase provides a Stagehand BYOB implementation behind it and
    48	measures recovery behavior plus the open agent-cache replay question.
    49	
    50	## Execution note (cross-repo)
    51	
    52	This spec lives in the HDP vault but its code phases execute in a clone of
    53	`emr-sync-driver`. Evidence and phase state record here
    54	(`vault/specs/emr-driver-tracer/`); the hub-feedback phase is the only one
    55	that edits HDP files (the research hub, via the vault worktree). Repo
    56	creation in the bootstrap phase is an irreversible op: main-session user
    57	sign-off, never delegated.
    58	
    59	## File manifest
    60	
    61	Single SoT is `tasks.yaml` `manifest:` (file -> new|modified -> purpose).
    62	Manifest paths are emr-sync-driver-relative except `vault/`-prefixed
    63	entries (HDP). For interface contracts (CLI signatures, data models, golden
    64	example, AC-mapped test manifest, behavior x backend matrix) see
    65	`reference/`.
    66	
    67	## Decisions
    68	
    69	Foundational decisions are NOT re-made here — they are user-ratified in the
    70	research hub's decision log (`vault/research/computer-use-emr-sync/state.yaml`,
    71	6 entries): DOM-first/vision-assist control loop, self-hosted pinned OpenEMR
    72	sandbox, structural security posture, taxonomy-from-spike-runs, Playwright +
    73	DBOS foundations, deployment topology. Duplicating them as ADRs would create
    74	mirror drift; this section records only spec-local decisions:
    75	
    76	- **Standalone driver, converge later** (interview Dim 3): the tracer
    77	  depends on no HDP package — HDP primitives are pre-trim shells and #11 is
    78	  in flight. The thin API is the convergence seam: its job operations are
    79	  the HTTP shape the `hh-emr-sync` adapter will consume, and the driver's
    80	  audit/checkpoint interfaces inform HDP's primitives from real usage.
    81	- **Fallback gated behind deterministic E2E** (interview Dim 2): the
    82	  deterministic skeleton must pass AC-003/AC-004 before any LLM-assist code
    83	  lands. Couples one unknown per phase; preserves the zero-LLM property of
    84	  the primary path as a tested invariant rather than a hope.
    85	- **Sessions are cattle** (from research, operationalized here):
    86	  storage_state is a bearer credential — custody rules in FR-009; on
    87	  session death the driver re-authenticates rather than persisting
    88	  long-lived session stores.
    89	- **Audit store is driver-local Postgres, not HDP's audit package**:
    90	  consequence of standalone-first. The event shape (models.py AuditEvent)
    91	  is written so a later HDP adapter can map it 1:1 into platform audit
    92	  primitives.
    93	
    94	## Risks
    95	
    96	- DBOS + Playwright interaction is unproven in this combination (async
    97	  Playwright inside DBOS steps; step granularity vs browser session
    98	  affinity). The tracer phase exists to surface exactly this class of
    99	  unknown early — if step-per-action is too chatty, the fallback design is
   100	  step-per-page-interaction with action-level audit retained.
   101	- OpenEMR compose specifics (ports, default creds, seeding) are known
   102	  unknowns resolved at bootstrap (hub open questions); they affect setup
   103	  cost, not architecture.
   104	- `connect_over_cdp` reattach topology (browser survives driver death) is
   105	  documented lower-fidelity; the tracer's SIGKILL test targets driver-process
   106	  death with browser relaunch + storage_state re-injection, which is the
   107	  supported path. Browser-process survival is an optimization, not a
   108	  requirement.

Accrues alongside the driver\nspike — a record, not a gating phase.\n\n## Situation\n\nMany EMR systems serving home health expose weak or no integration APIs.\n`hh-emr-sync` today declares only `httpx` as its transport dependency,\npresuming an API that many target systems lack (GH #14). OpenEMR is already\nknown to this vault as a schema-design reference [ai-found: raw/01]; here it\nreappears in a different role — a real EMR UI to automate against.\n\n## Complication\n\nBrowser-level automation (DOM-driven, vision-assisted) is a credible\nadditional transport for API-poor targets, but credentialed browser sessions\nagainst a medical-records UI carry a threat model that HTTP clients do not:\nprompt injection from rendered content, credential exposure, and a long tail\nof workflow failure modes (session death, selector drift, latency cliffs,\npartial write-back). The driver must be credible *infrastructure*, not a demo.\n\n## Question\n\nWhat does a browser-level EMR sync transport need to be credible\ninfrastructure: how are credentialed sessions secured, which sandbox grounds\nthe work, and how do long-running browser workflows against EMR UIs actually\nfail?\n\n## Approach\n\nTwo gather waves on 2026-06-11 (see `state.yaml` for the plan). Wave one:\nprior vault context, the OpenEMR public demo page, OpenEMR Docker self-hosting\ndocs, and Anthropic's computer-use security/limitations documentation. Wave\ntwo (build-vs-adopt): framework evaluations of the Stagehand Python SDK,\nbrowser-use, Skyvern, and Playwright, plus cloud deployment options — each\nevaluated against the wave-one decisions rather than in the abstract. The\nfailure taxonomy below is a seed structure — its rows accrue from tracer-spike\nruns in the driver repository, each observed class feeding retry/idempotency/\nobservability design.\n\n## Findings\n\n### Security posture\n\nGrounded in the vendor's own guidance for computer-use agents\n[ai-found: raw/04]:\n\n1. **Synthetic data only.** The sandbox holds zero real patient data, ever.\n   This is scope, not mitigation — there is no failure mode in which PHI is\n   exposed because no PHI exists in the loop.\n2. **Container isolation, minimal privileges.** The driver and the browser it\n   controls run in a dedicated container/VM (\"dedicated virtual machine or\n   container with minimal privileges\" — raw/04). The Anthropic reference\n   implementation itself is Docker-contained.\n3. **Network allowlist.** The browser environment can reach the sandbox EMR\n   and nothing else (\"limiting internet access to an allowlist of domains\" —\n   raw/04). An injected instruction cannot exfiltrate to a host it cannot\n   resolve.\n4. **Credentials outside the model loop.** DOM-first automation performs\n   login programmatically (selectors + secret store), so credentials never\n   enter a prompt. The vendor path of last resort — credentials in prompt XML\n   tags — is documented to increase prompt-injection blast radius (raw/04);\n   the DOM-first default avoids it structurally.\n5. **Session/audit boundary.** Every driver action that mutates EMR state is\n   logged as an auditable event; write-back operations carry idempotency keys\n   so a replay after partial failure cannot double-apply. This is where the\n   driver meets HDP's audit/provenance primitives.\n6. **HITL gates on consequential writes.** Human confirmation before\n   meaningful real-world consequences (raw/04) aligns with HDP's existing\n   confidence-gated HITL design — the transport inherits the platform's\n   review checkpoint rather than inventing its own.\n7. **Prompt-injection stance.** Rendered EMR content is untrusted input.\n   Defense in depth: DOM-first control (the model is not steering from\n   screenshots in the default path), Anthropic's screenshot classifiers when\n   vision assist is active, allowlisted egress, and HITL gates — the docs are\n   explicit that precautions remain necessary even with the classifier layer\n   (raw/04).\n\n### Sandbox selection — self-hosted OpenEMR (decision)\n\n**Decision: self-hosted OpenEMR via the official Docker production compose,\nversion-pinned.** [ai-found: raw/02, raw/03]\n\n| Criterion | Public demo (`demo.openemr.io`) | Self-hosted Docker |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| State persistence | Wiped daily at 8:00 UTC | We control reset timing |\n| Isolation | Shared with other visitors | Single-tenant |\n| Authorization for automated traffic | No AUP stated either way | Our infrastructure |\n| Version stability | Tracks upstream | Pinned (e.g. `7.0.3`) |\n| Synthetic patients | Two portal patients guaranteed | Seeded deliberately |\n| Setup cost | Zero | `docker compose up`, ~5-10 min, arm64-capable |\n\nThe daily wipe alone disqualifies the public demo for failure-taxonomy work —\nmulti-day observation of session death and drift requires state we own. The\ndemo remains useful for quick manual UI recon. Gap to resolve at spike time:\ndefault ports/credentials and synthetic-data loading live in the Docker Hub\npage/compose files, not DOCKER_README.md (raw/03).\n\n### DOM-first, vision-assist (decision)\n\n**Decision: DOM-driven automation is the primary control loop; vision is\nassist and fallback.** The vendor's own limitation list argues for this\n[ai-found: raw/04]: latency \"too slow compared to regular human-directed\ncomputer actions,\" coordinate hallucination in vision-driven clicking,\nscrolling unreliability, and degraded reliability against niche applications\n— EMR UIs being exactly that. DOM selectors are deterministic, fast, cheap,\nand auditable (a selector either matched or it didn't; a logged action replay\nis exact). Vision assist earns its place where the DOM fails: canvas-rendered\nor legacy widgets, selector-drift recovery (visually re-locating a control\nwhose selector broke), and CAPTCHAs-class anomalies that should halt for human\nreview anyway.\n\n### Failure taxonomy (seed)\n\nClasses named in #18; rows accrue from spike runs in the driver repo. vault/specs/emr-driver-tracer/evidence/interview/codex-interview-challenger-raw.json:16:{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_7","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/zsh -lc 'rtk read vault/research/computer-use-emr-sync/README.md'","aggregated_output":"---\nid: computer-use-emr-sync\ntitle: Computer-use as an EMR sync transport\ntype: research\nstatus: proposed\ncreated: 2026-06-11\nupdated: 2026-06-11\nhub: computer-use-emr-sync\nparent_hub: null\nowner: peterkc\naudience: [driver-repo implementers, hh-emr-sync adapter design]\ndirection: exploring\ntags: [computer-use, emr-sync, security, sandbox, home-health]\nrelated: []\n---\n\n# Computer-use as an EMR sync transport\n\nLiving hub for GitHub #18 (parent epic #14). Accrues alongside the driver\nspike — a record, not a gating phase.\n\n## Situation\n\nMany EMR systems serving home health expose weak or no integration APIs.\n`hh-emr-sync` today declares only `httpx` as its transport dependency,\npresuming an API that many target systems lack (GH #14). OpenEMR is already\nknown to this vault as a schema-design reference [ai-found: raw/01]; here it\nreappears in a different role — a real EMR UI to automate against.\n\n## Complication\n\nBrowser-level automation (DOM-driven, vision-assisted) is a credible\nadditional transport for API-poor targets, but credentialed browser sessions\nagainst a medical-records UI carry a threat model that HTTP clients do not:\nprompt injection from rendered content, credential exposure, and a long tail\nof workflow failure modes (session death, selector drift, latency cliffs,\npartial write-back). The driver must be credible *infrastructure*, not a demo.\n\n## Question\n\nWhat does a browser-level EMR sync transport need to be credible\ninfrastructure: how are credentialed sessions secured, which sandbox grounds\nthe work, and how do long-running browser workflows against EMR UIs actually\nfail?\n\n## Approach\n\nTwo gather waves on 2026-06-11 (see `state.yaml` for the plan). Wave one:\nprior vault context, the OpenEMR public demo page, OpenEMR Docker self-hosting\ndocs, and Anthropic's computer-use security/limitations documentation. Wave\ntwo (build-vs-adopt): framework evaluations of the Stagehand Python SDK,\nbrowser-use, Skyvern, and Playwright, plus cloud deployment options — each\nevaluated against the wave-one decisions rather than in the abstract. The\nfailure taxonomy below is a seed structure — its rows accrue from tracer-spike\nruns in the driver repository, each observed class feeding retry/idempotency/\nobservability design.\n\n## Findings\n\n### Security posture\n\nGrounded in the vendor's own guidance for computer-use agents\n[ai-found: raw/04]:\n\n1. **Synthetic data only.** The sandbox holds zero real patient data, ever.\n   This is scope, not mitigation — there is no failure mode in which PHI is\n   exposed because no PHI exists in the loop.\n2. **Container isolation, minimal privileges.** The driver and the browser it\n   controls run in a dedicated container/VM (\"dedicated virtual machine or\n   container with minimal privileges\" — raw/04). The Anthropic reference\n   implementation itself is Docker-contained.\n3. **Network allowlist.** The browser environment can reach the sandbox EMR\n   and nothing else (\"limiting internet access to an allowlist of domains\" —\n   raw/04). An injected instruction cannot exfiltrate to a host it cannot\n   resolve.\n4. **Credentials outside the model loop.** DOM-first automation performs\n   login programmatically (selectors + secret store), so credentials never\n   enter a prompt. The vendor path of last resort — credentials in prompt XML\n   tags — is documented to increase prompt-injection blast radius (raw/04);\n   the DOM-first default avoids it structurally.\n5. **Session/audit boundary.** Every driver action that mutates EMR state is\n   logged as an auditable event; write-back operations carry idempotency keys\n   so a replay after partial failure cannot double-apply. This is where the\n   driver meets HDP's audit/provenance primitives.\n6. **HITL gates on consequential writes.** Human confirmation before\n   meaningful real-world consequences (raw/04) aligns with HDP's existing\n   confidence-gated HITL design — the transport inherits the platform's\n   review checkpoint rather than inventing its own.\n7. **Prompt-injection stance.** Rendered EMR content is untrusted input.\n   Defense in depth: DOM-first control (the model is not steering from\n   screenshots in the default path), Anthropic's screenshot classifiers when\n   vision assist is active, allowlisted egress, and HITL gates — the docs are\n   explicit that precautions remain necessary even with the classifier layer\n   (raw/04).\n\n### Sandbox selection — self-hosted OpenEMR (decision)\n\n**Decision: self-hosted OpenEMR via the official Docker production compose,\nversion-pinned.** [ai-found: raw/02, raw/03]\n\n| Criterion | Public demo (`demo.openemr.io`) | Self-hosted Docker |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| State persistence | Wiped daily at 8:00 UTC | We control reset timing |\n| Isolation | Shared with other visitors | Single-tenant |\n| Authorization for automated traffic | No AUP stated either way | Our infrastructure |\n| Version stability | Tracks upstream | Pinned (e.g. `7.0.3`) |\n| Synthetic patients | Two portal patients guaranteed | Seeded deliberately |\n| Setup cost | Zero | `docker compose up`, ~5-10 min, arm64-capable |\n\nThe daily wipe alone disqualifies the public demo for failure-taxonomy work —\nmulti-day observation of session death and drift requires state we own. The\ndemo remains useful for quick manual UI recon. Gap to resolve at spike time:\ndefault ports/credentials and synthetic-data loading live in the Docker Hub\npage/compose files, not DOCKER_README.md (raw/03).\n\n### DOM-first, vision-assist (decision)\n\n**Decision: DOM-driven automation is the primary control loop; vision is\nassist and fallback.** The vendor's own limitation list argues for this\n[ai-found: raw/04]: latency \"too slow compared to regular human-directed\ncomputer actions,\" coordinate hallucination in vision-driven clicking,\nscrolling unreliability, and degraded reliability against niche applications\n— EMR UIs being exactly that. DOM selectors are deterministic, fast, cheap,\nand auditable (a selector either matched or it didn't; a logged action replay\nis exact). Vision assist earns its place where the DOM fails: canvas-rendered\nor legacy widgets, selector-drift recovery (visually re-locating a control\nwhose selector broke), and CAPTCHAs-class anomalies that should halt for human\nreview anyway.\n\n### Failure taxonomy (seed)\n\nClasses named in #18; rows accrue from spike runs in the driver repo. Each\nobserved failure gets: detection signal, blast radius, hardening\nrecommendation.\n\n| Class | What it looks like | Hardening direction (hypothesis) |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Session death | Auth timeout/logout mid-workflow | Checkpointed orchestration; re-auth + resume from last checkpoint |\n| Selector drift | EMR update changes DOM; selectors stop matching | Versioned selector maps; vision-assisted re-location; drift alarms |\n| Latency cliffs | Page loads stall; waits time out unpredictably | Adaptive timeouts; circuit breakers; observability on wait distributions |\n| Partial write-back | Multi-field form submit interrupted midway | Idempotency keys; read-after-write verification; transactional batching where the UI allows |\n\nThe infrastructure interest is in this column structure — retries,\nidempotent write-back, checkpointed orchestration, observability — more than\nin any single extraction's accuracy.\n\n### Build-vs-adopt: framework evaluation (decision, proposed)\n\n**Decision: build the driver on Playwright (deterministic loop) + DBOS\n(durable checkpoint/resume); evaluate Stagehand's BYOB pattern for the\nLLM-fallback layer during the spike; borrow browser-use's DOM serialization\nand Skyvern's failure semantics as reference architecture, not dependencies.**\n[ai-found: raw/05, raw/06, raw/07; durable execution raw/08]\n\nThe 2026 production consensus independently converged on the hub's wave-one\ncontrol-loop decision: deterministic DOM code primary, LLM engaged only where\nthe page is unpredictable. Evaluated against that decision:\n\n| Candidate | License | Verdict | Why |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Playwright (Python) | Apache-2.0 | **Adopt** — deterministic engine | Auto-waiting, storage_state login reuse, per-action traces, CDP reconnect (browser survives driver restart); no disqualifiers. Gap list (audit log, re-auth loop, step retry, egress enforcement) is the driver's actual product surface |\n| DBOS Transact | MIT | **Adopt** — checkpoint/resume layer | Embedded Python library, Postgres-backed (matches stack); crash-resume from last completed step; collapses workflow engine + queue + idempotency ledger into one component |\n| Stagehand Python SDK | MIT (SDK + server) | **Evaluate in spike** — fallback layer | BYOB maps exactly onto DOM-first/LLM-fallback (own Playwright page passes into `observe/act/extract`); fully self-hostable via embedded open-source server. Frictions: Node server sidecar, Python SDK lacks act-level caching/self-heal the TS original has |\n| browser-use | MIT (core) | **Reference / possible component** | Indexed-element DOM serializer is the best off-the-shelf page representation for drift recovery and is callable standalone; but pre-1.0 with two foundation swaps in 18 months, and its deterministic-replay sister project (workflow-use) is early-stage and AGPL |\n| Skyvern | AGPL-3.0 | **Reference architecture only** | LLM-per-step control loop inverts the ratified decision; AGPL bars a hard dependency in an MIT driver repo. Worth reading: stable-ID element tree + annotated-screenshot grounding, mutation-observer drift detection, workflow failure semantics (`continue_on_failure`, error-code mapping, human-pause blocks) |\n\nWhat remains in-house — and is the differentiating surface, not incidental\nglue: versioned selector maps, EMR workflow definitions, read-after-write\nverification, the structured PHI-minimal audit log, failure classification\n(one `TimeoutError` → dead-session vs latency vs drift), and the\n`hh-emr-sync` adapter contract. Notably, no evaluated framework ships durable\ncheckpoint/resume for long-running jobs — confirming the seam the wave-one\ncontract analysis identified.\n\n### Cloud deployment (decision, proposed)\n\n**Decision: spike runs local/single-VM (synthetic data — anywhere works);\nthe production-shaped reference topology is self-hosted workers on a\nBAA-covered cloud, with managed browser infrastructure recorded as a\ncredible alternative.** [ai-found: raw/08]\n\nSelf-hosted shape: container workers (ECS Fargate-class — no runtime limits,\n~2 GB per browser task) pulling jobs from the Postgres-backed queue;\ncheckpoint store and outbox in the same Postgres; secrets manager for EMR\ncredentials; VPC egress allowlist enforced at the network layer (the\nwave-one posture's structural control, in cloud terms); LLM-assist calls\nrouted through a BAA-covered model platform so even fallback screenshots\nstay inside one compliance boundary. One practical constraint shapes the\ntopology: EMR and payer portals frequently allowlist source IPs, so egress\nmust present a static IP (NAT/pinned proxy) — native to a VPC, awkward for\nrotating managed fleets.\n\nManaged alternative: Browserbase (the infrastructure behind Stagehand)\ndocuments SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA BAAs on request, a zero-data-retention mode,\nand per-session dedicated VMs — so the managed path is compliance-viable,\ntrading vendor dependency for isolation engineering not built in-house. The\nspike costs nothing to keep portable across both: the driver talks to a CDP\nendpoint either way.\n\n## Synthesis\n\nA credible browser-level EMR sync transport is **a hardened, audited,\nDOM-first driver running against owned, synthetic-only infrastructure** — not\na vision-loop agent pointed at a shared demo. The security posture is mostly\nstructural (isolation, allowlist, credentials outside the model loop,\nsynthetic-only scope) rather than behavioral, which is what makes it\ndefensible. The sandbox decision (self-hosted, pinned OpenEMR) follows from\nneeding multi-day failure state; the DOM-first decision follows from the\nvendor's own limitation list. What remains genuinely open — how these\nworkflows fail in practice — is empirical, and the taxonomy table is the\ninstrument for capturing it.\n\nAdapter-contract implications for the `hh-emr-sync` seam (#11): the contract\nmust accommodate idempotency keys, checkpoint/resume semantics, and\nasynchronous completion — an HTTP adapter satisfies these trivially; an\nautomation adapter requires them. If the seam bakes in synchronous\nrequest/response, the automation transport will not slot in.\n\nThe build-vs-adopt pass narrows what the driver repository actually is:\nfoundations are adoptable (Playwright for the deterministic loop, DBOS for\ndurability), so the repository's own code concentrates on the domain layer —\nselector maps, workflow definitions, audit, failure classification, and the\nadapter contract. That is the right shape for a tracer-bullet project: the\ncustom code is exactly the part with research value.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Driver repository: name and visibility (pending owner decision); hub links\n  out once created.\n- OpenEMR synthetic-patient seeding: best mechanism (built-in demo data vs\n  Synthea import) — resolve at spike time.\n- Default ports/credentials for the production compose — Docker Hub page.\n- Which OASIS-relevant OpenEMR workflows make the first tracer target (visit\n  documentation? assessment forms?).\n- Stagehand Python: does the agent-level cache entry have a server-side\n  replay-submission path, or is replay fully client-built? (raw/05 flags\n  UNVERIFIED) — measure during the spike's fallback evaluation.\n\n## Next actions\n\n- Create the driver repository (Playwright + DBOS scaffold per the\n  build-vs-adopt decision); first tracer run against self-hosted OpenEMR.\n- Begin populating taxonomy rows from observed failures (one hardening\n  recommendation per observed class — #18 exit condition).\n- Feed adapter-contract implications into the #11 trim spec's emr-sync seam.\n\n## Cross-references\n\n- `state.yaml` — structured state for AI re-load\n- `raw/` — per-source captures (01 vault context, 02 demo page, 03 Docker\n  docs, 04 Anthropic security, 05 Stagehand Python, 06 browser-use + Skyvern,\n  07 Playwright, 08 cloud deployment)\n- GitHub: #18 (this spike), #14 (parent epic), #11 (adapter seam)\n- `../references.md` #9 — OpenEMR as schema reference (distinct role)\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

     2	
     3	## Architecture
     4	
     5	The driver is the production skeleton of a browser-level EMR sync transport,
     6	built as the thinnest end-to-end thread that exercises every load-bearing
     7	joint: durable job orchestration, deterministic browser control, audit,
     8	failure classification, and the two integration surfaces (CLI, thin API).
     9	Extraction quality and OASIS modeling are explicitly not this system's
    10	concern — the infrastructure is.
    11	
    12	```
    13	  CLI (typer)            thin API (FastAPI)
    14	      |                        |
    15	      +----------+------------+
    16	                 v
    17	        DBOS workflow (field-roundtrip job)
    18	        each step checkpointed in Postgres
    19	        write steps carry idempotency keys
    20	                 |
    21	                 v
    22	        browser session (Playwright, Chromium)
    23	        programmatic login -> storage_state custody
    24	        egress: default-deny route() allowlist
    25	                 |                          |
    26	                 v                          v
    27	        selector map (versioned)      audit store (append-only)
    28	        miss -> failures.classify()   every action, replayable
    29	        drift -> fallback seam
    30	        (Stagehand BYOB, gated phase)
    31	                 |
    32	                 v
    33	        OpenEMR sandbox (docker-compose, pinned, synthetic-only)
    34	```
    35	
    36	Job lifecycle: a job submitted via CLI or API becomes a DBOS workflow; each
    37	browser interaction is a step whose completion is checkpointed. A killed
    38	driver resumes from the last completed step — completed writes are not
    39	re-applied because write steps consult their idempotency key before acting.
    40	Every action (including blocked egress and failures) appends an audit
    41	event; replay is a read of that stream in order. Failure classification
    42	runs before any retry decision so the taxonomy data is captured even when
    43	recovery succeeds.
    44	
    45	The fallback seam is a driver-owned Protocol: the deterministic path never
    46	imports or calls it (zero LLM calls, asserted by AC-011); the gated
    47	fallback-eval phase provides a Stagehand BYOB implementation behind it and
    48	measures recovery behavior plus the open agent-cache replay question.
    49	
    50	## Execution note (cross-repo)
    51	
    52	This spec lives in the HDP vault but its code phases execute in a clone of
    53	`emr-sync-driver`. Evidence and phase state record here
    54	(`vault/specs/emr-driver-tracer/`); the hub-feedback phase is the only one
    55	that edits HDP files (the research hub, via the vault worktree). Repo
    56	creation in the bootstrap phase is an irreversible op: main-session user
    57	sign-off, never delegated.
    58	
    59	## File manifest
    60	
    61	Single SoT is `tasks.yaml` `manifest:` (file -> new|modified -> purpose).
    62	Manifest paths are emr-sync-driver-relative except `vault/`-prefixed
    63	entries (HDP). For interface contracts (CLI signatures, data models, golden
    64	example, AC-mapped test manifest, behavior x backend matrix) see
    65	`reference/`.
    66	
    67	## Decisions
    68	
    69	Foundational decisions are NOT re-made here — they are user-ratified in the
    70	research hub's decision log (`vault/research/computer-use-emr-sync/state.yaml`,
    71	6 entries): DOM-first/vision-assist control loop, self-hosted pinned OpenEMR
    72	sandbox, structural security posture, taxonomy-from-spike-runs, Playwright +
    73	DBOS foundations, deployment topology. Duplicating them as ADRs would create
    74	mirror drift; this section records only spec-local decisions:
    75	
    76	- **Standalone driver, converge later** (interview Dim 3): the tracer
    77	  depends on no HDP package — HDP primitives are pre-trim shells and #11 is
    78	  in flight. The thin API is the convergence seam: its job operations are
    79	  the HTTP shape the `hh-emr-sync` adapter will consume, and the driver's
    80	  audit/checkpoint interfaces inform HDP's primitives from real usage.
    81	- **Fallback gated behind deterministic E2E** (interview Dim 2): the
    82	  deterministic skeleton must pass AC-003/AC-004 before any LLM-assist code
    83	  lands. Couples one unknown per phase; preserves the zero-LLM property of
    84	  the primary path as a tested invariant rather than a hope.
    85	- **Sessions are cattle** (from research, operationalized here):
    86	  storage_state is a bearer credential — custody rules in FR-009; on
    87	  session death the driver re-authenticates rather than persisting
    88	  long-lived session stores.
    89	- **Audit store is driver-local Postgres, not HDP's audit package**:
    90	  consequence of standalone-first. The event shape (models.py AuditEvent)
    91	  is written so a later HDP adapter can map it 1:1 into platform audit
    92	  primitives.
    93	
    94	## Risks
    95	
    96	- DBOS + Playwright interaction is unproven in this combination (async
    97	  Playwright inside DBOS steps; step granularity vs browser session
    98	  affinity). The tracer phase exists to surface exactly this class of
    99	  unknown early — if step-per-action is too chatty, the fallback design is
   100	  step-per-page-interaction with action-level audit retained.
   101	- OpenEMR compose specifics (ports, default creds, seeding) are known
   102	  unknowns resolved at bootstrap (hub open questions); they affect setup
   103	  cost, not architecture.
   104	- `connect_over_cdp` reattach topology (browser survives driver death) is
   105	  documented lower-fidelity; the tracer's SIGKILL test targets driver-process
   106	  death with browser relaunch + storage_state re-injection, which is the
   107	  supported path. Browser-process survival is an optimization, not a
   108	  requirement.

Accrues alongside the driver\nspike — a record, not a gating phase.\n\n## Situation\n\nMany EMR systems serving home health expose weak or no integration APIs.\n`hh-emr-sync` today declares only `httpx` as its transport dependency,\npresuming an API that many target systems lack (GH #14). OpenEMR is already\nknown to this vault as a schema-design reference [ai-found: raw/01]; here it\nreappears in a different role — a real EMR UI to automate against.\n\n## Complication\n\nBrowser-level automation (DOM-driven, vision-assisted) is a credible\nadditional transport for API-poor targets, but credentialed browser sessions\nagainst a medical-records UI carry a threat model that HTTP clients do not:\nprompt injection from rendered content, credential exposure, and a long tail\nof workflow failure modes (session death, selector drift, latency cliffs,\npartial write-back). The driver must be credible *infrastructure*, not a demo.\n\n## Question\n\nWhat does a browser-level EMR sync transport need to be credible\ninfrastructure: how are credentialed sessions secured, which sandbox grounds\nthe work, and how do long-running browser workflows against EMR UIs actually\nfail?\n\n## Approach\n\nTwo gather waves on 2026-06-11 (see `state.yaml` for the plan). Wave one:\nprior vault context, the OpenEMR public demo page, OpenEMR Docker self-hosting\ndocs, and Anthropic's computer-use security/limitations documentation. Wave\ntwo (build-vs-adopt): framework evaluations of the Stagehand Python SDK,\nbrowser-use, Skyvern, and Playwright, plus cloud deployment options — each\nevaluated against the wave-one decisions rather than in the abstract. The\nfailure taxonomy below is a seed structure — its rows accrue from tracer-spike\nruns in the driver repository, each observed class feeding retry/idempotency/\nobservability design.\n\n## Findings\n\n### Security posture\n\nGrounded in the vendor's own guidance for computer-use agents\n[ai-found: raw/04]:\n\n1. **Synthetic data only.** The sandbox holds zero real patient data, ever.\n   This is scope, not mitigation — there is no failure mode in which PHI is\n   exposed because no PHI exists in the loop.\n2. **Container isolation, minimal privileges.** The driver and the browser it\n   controls run in a dedicated container/VM (\"dedicated virtual machine or\n   container with minimal privileges\" — raw/04). The Anthropic reference\n   implementation itself is Docker-contained.\n3. **Network allowlist.** The browser environment can reach the sandbox EMR\n   and nothing else (\"limiting internet access to an allowlist of domains\" —\n   raw/04). An injected instruction cannot exfiltrate to a host it cannot\n   resolve.\n4. **Credentials outside the model loop.** DOM-first automation performs\n   login programmatically (selectors + secret store), so credentials never\n   enter a prompt. The vendor path of last resort — credentials in prompt XML\n   tags — is documented to increase prompt-injection blast radius (raw/04);\n   the DOM-first default avoids it structurally.\n5. **Session/audit boundary.** Every driver action that mutates EMR state is\n   logged as an auditable event; write-back operations carry idempotency keys\n   so a replay after partial failure cannot double-apply. This is where the\n   driver meets HDP's audit/provenance primitives.\n6. **HITL gates on consequential writes.** Human confirmation before\n   meaningful real-world consequences (raw/04) aligns with HDP's existing\n   confidence-gated HITL design — the transport inherits the platform's\n   review checkpoint rather than inventing its own.\n7. **Prompt-injection stance.** Rendered EMR content is untrusted input.\n   Defense in depth: DOM-first control (the model is not steering from\n   screenshots in the default path), Anthropic's screenshot classifiers when\n   vision assist is active, allowlisted egress, and HITL gates — the docs are\n   explicit that precautions remain necessary even with the classifier layer\n   (raw/04).\n\n### Sandbox selection — self-hosted OpenEMR (decision)\n\n**Decision: self-hosted OpenEMR via the official Docker production compose,\nversion-pinned.** [ai-found: raw/02, raw/03]\n\n| Criterion | Public demo (`demo.openemr.io`) | Self-hosted Docker |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| State persistence | Wiped daily at 8:00 UTC | We control reset timing |\n| Isolation | Shared with other visitors | Single-tenant |\n| Authorization for automated traffic | No AUP stated either way | Our infrastructure |\n| Version stability | Tracks upstream | Pinned (e.g. `7.0.3`) |\n| Synthetic patients | Two portal patients guaranteed | Seeded deliberately |\n| Setup cost | Zero | `docker compose up`, ~5-10 min, arm64-capable |\n\nThe daily wipe alone disqualifies the public demo for failure-taxonomy work —\nmulti-day observation of session death and drift requires state we own. The\ndemo remains useful for quick manual UI recon. Gap to resolve at spike time:\ndefault ports/credentials and synthetic-data loading live in the Docker Hub\npage/compose files, not DOCKER_README.md (raw/03).\n\n### DOM-first, vision-assist (decision)\n\n**Decision: DOM-driven automation is the primary control loop; vision is\nassist and fallback.** The vendor's own limitation list argues for this\n[ai-found: raw/04]: latency \"too slow compared to regular human-directed\ncomputer actions,\" coordinate hallucination in vision-driven clicking,\nscrolling unreliability, and degraded reliability against niche applications\n— EMR UIs being exactly that. DOM selectors are deterministic, fast, cheap,\nand auditable (a selector either matched or it didn't; a logged action replay\nis exact). Vision assist earns its place where the DOM fails: canvas-rendered\nor legacy widgets, selector-drift recovery (visually re-locating a control\nwhose selector broke), and CAPTCHAs-class anomalies that should halt for human\nreview anyway.\n\n### Failure taxonomy (seed)\n\nClasses named in #18; rows accrue from spike runs in the driver repo. Each\nobserved failure gets: detection signal, blast radius, hardening\nrecommendation.\n\n| Class | What it looks like | Hardening direction (hypothesis) |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Session death | Auth timeout/logout mid-workflow | Checkpointed orchestration; re-auth + resume from last checkpoint |\n| Selector drift | EMR update changes DOM; selectors stop matching | Versioned selector maps; vision-assisted re-location; drift alarms |\n| Latency cliffs | Page loads stall; waits time out unpredictably | Adaptive timeouts; circuit breakers; observability on wait distributions |\n| Partial write-back | Multi-field form submit interrupted midway | Idempotency keys; read-after-write verification; transactional batching where the UI allows |\n\nThe infrastructure interest is in this column structure — retries,\nidempotent write-back, checkpointed orchestration, observability — more than\nin any single extraction's accuracy.\n\n### Build-vs-adopt: framework evaluation (decision, proposed)\n\n**Decision: build the driver on Playwright (deterministic loop) + DBOS\n(durable checkpoint/resume); evaluate Stagehand's BYOB pattern for the\nLLM-fallback layer during the spike; borrow browser-use's DOM serialization\nand Skyvern's failure semantics as reference architecture, not dependencies.**\n[ai-found: raw/05, raw/06, raw/07; durable execution raw/08]\n\nThe 2026 production consensus independently converged on the hub's wave-one\ncontrol-loop decision: deterministic DOM code primary, LLM engaged only where\nthe page is unpredictable. Evaluated against that decision:\n\n| Candidate | License | Verdict | Why |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Playwright (Python) | Apache-2.0 | **Adopt** — deterministic engine | Auto-waiting, storage_state login reuse, per-action traces, CDP reconnect (browser survives driver restart); no disqualifiers. Gap list (audit log, re-auth loop, step retry, egress enforcement) is the driver's actual product surface |\n| DBOS Transact | MIT | **Adopt** — checkpoint/resume layer | Embedded Python library, Postgres-backed (matches stack); crash-resume from last completed step; collapses workflow engine + queue + idempotency ledger into one component |\n| Stagehand Python SDK | MIT (SDK + server) | **Evaluate in spike** — fallback layer | BYOB maps exactly onto DOM-first/LLM-fallback (own Playwright page passes into `observe/act/extract`); fully self-hostable via embedded open-source server. Frictions: Node server sidecar, Python SDK lacks act-level caching/self-heal the TS original has |\n| browser-use | MIT (core) | **Reference / possible component** | Indexed-element DOM serializer is the best off-the-shelf page representation for drift recovery and is callable standalone; but pre-1.0 with two foundation swaps in 18 months, and its deterministic-replay sister project (workflow-use) is early-stage and AGPL |\n| Skyvern | AGPL-3.0 | **Reference architecture only** | LLM-per-step control loop inverts the ratified decision; AGPL bars a hard dependency in an MIT driver repo. Worth reading: stable-ID element tree + annotated-screenshot grounding, mutation-observer drift detection, workflow failure semantics (`continue_on_failure`, error-code mapping, human-pause blocks) |\n\nWhat remains in-house — and is the differentiating surface, not incidental\nglue: versioned selector maps, EMR workflow definitions, read-after-write\nverification, the structured PHI-minimal audit log, failure classification\n(one `TimeoutError` → dead-session vs latency vs drift), and the\n`hh-emr-sync` adapter contract. Notably, no evaluated framework ships durable\ncheckpoint/resume for long-running jobs — confirming the seam the wave-one\ncontract analysis identified.\n\n### Cloud deployment (decision, proposed)\n\n**Decision: spike runs local/single-VM (synthetic data — anywhere works);\nthe production-shaped reference topology is self-hosted workers on a\nBAA-covered cloud, with managed browser infrastructure recorded as a\ncredible alternative.** [ai-found: raw/08]\n\nSelf-hosted shape: container workers (ECS Fargate-class — no runtime limits,\n~2 GB per browser task) pulling jobs from the Postgres-backed queue;\ncheckpoint store and outbox in the same Postgres; secrets manager for EMR\ncredentials; VPC egress allowlist enforced at the network layer (the\nwave-one posture's structural control, in cloud terms); LLM-assist calls\nrouted through a BAA-covered model platform so even fallback screenshots\nstay inside one compliance boundary. One practical constraint shapes the\ntopology: EMR and payer portals frequently allowlist source IPs, so egress\nmust present a static IP (NAT/pinned proxy) — native to a VPC, awkward for\nrotating managed fleets.\n\nManaged alternative: Browserbase (the infrastructure behind Stagehand)\ndocuments SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA BAAs on request, a zero-data-retention mode,\nand per-session dedicated VMs — so the managed path is compliance-viable,\ntrading vendor dependency for isolation engineering not built in-house. The\nspike costs nothing to keep portable across both: the driver talks to a CDP\nendpoint either way.\n\n## Synthesis\n\nA credible browser-level EMR sync transport is **a hardened, audited,\nDOM-first driver running against owned, synthetic-only infrastructure** — not\na vision-loop agent pointed at a shared demo. The security posture is mostly\nstructural (isolation, allowlist, credentials outside the model loop,\nsynthetic-only scope) rather than behavioral, which is what makes it\ndefensible. The sandbox decision (self-hosted, pinned OpenEMR) follows from\nneeding multi-day failure state; the DOM-first decision follows from the\nvendor's own limitation list. What remains genuinely open — how these\nworkflows fail in practice — is empirical, and the taxonomy table is the\ninstrument for capturing it.\n\nAdapter-contract implications for the `hh-emr-sync` seam (#11): the contract\nmust accommodate idempotency keys, checkpoint/resume semantics, and\nasynchronous completion — an HTTP adapter satisfies these trivially; an\nautomation adapter requires them. If the seam bakes in synchronous\nrequest/response, the automation transport will not slot in.\n\nThe build-vs-adopt pass narrows what the driver repository actually is:\nfoundations are adoptable (Playwright for the deterministic loop, DBOS for\ndurability), so the repository's own code concentrates on the domain layer —\nselector maps, workflow definitions, audit, failure classification, and the\nadapter contract. That is the right shape for a tracer-bullet project: the\ncustom code is exactly the part with research value.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Driver repository: name and visibility (pending owner decision); hub links\n  out once created.\n- OpenEMR synthetic-patient seeding: best mechanism (built-in demo data vs\n  Synthea import) — resolve at spike time.\n- Default ports/credentials for the production compose — Docker Hub page.\n- Which OASIS-relevant OpenEMR workflows make the first tracer target (visit\n  documentation? assessment forms?).\n- Stagehand Python: does the agent-level cache entry have a server-side\n  replay-submission path, or is replay fully client-built? (raw/05 flags\n  UNVERIFIED) — measure during the spike's fallback evaluation.\n\n## Next actions\n\n- Create the driver repository (Playwright + DBOS scaffold per the\n  build-vs-adopt decision); first tracer run against self-hosted OpenEMR.\n- Begin populating taxonomy rows from observed failures (one hardening\n  recommendation per observed class — #18 exit condition).\n- Feed adapter-contract implications into the #11 trim spec's emr-sync seam.\n\n## Cross-references\n\n- `state.yaml` — structured state for AI re-load\n- `raw/` — per-source captures (01 vault context, 02 demo page, 03 Docker\n  docs, 04 Anthropic security, 05 Stagehand Python, 06 browser-use + Skyvern,\n  07 Playwright, 08 cloud deployment)\n- GitHub: #18 (this spike), #14 (parent epic), #11 (adapter seam)\n- `../references.md` #9 — OpenEMR as schema reference (distinct role)\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
