vault/specs/emr-driver-tracer/evidence/interview/codex-interview-challenger-raw.json:16:{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_7","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/zsh -lc 'rtk read vault/research/computer-use-emr-sync/README.md'","aggregated_output":"---\nid: computer-use-emr-sync\ntitle: Computer-use as an EMR sync transport\ntype: research\nstatus: proposed\ncreated: 2026-06-11\nupdated: 2026-06-11\nhub: computer-use-emr-sync\nparent_hub: null\nowner: peterkc\naudience: [driver-repo implementers, hh-emr-sync adapter design]\ndirection: exploring\ntags: [computer-use, emr-sync, security, sandbox, home-health]\nrelated: []\n---\n\n# Computer-use as an EMR sync transport\n\nLiving hub for GitHub #18 (parent epic #14). Accrues alongside the driver\nspike — a record, not a gating phase.\n\n## Situation\n\nMany EMR systems serving home health expose weak or no integration APIs.\n`hh-emr-sync` today declares only `httpx` as its transport dependency,\npresuming an API that many target systems lack (GH #14). OpenEMR is already\nknown to this vault as a schema-design reference [ai-found: raw/01]; here it\nreappears in a different role — a real EMR UI to automate against.\n\n## Complication\n\nBrowser-level automation (DOM-driven, vision-assisted) is a credible\nadditional transport for API-poor targets, but credentialed browser sessions\nagainst a medical-records UI carry a threat model that HTTP clients do not:\nprompt injection from rendered content, credential exposure, and a long tail\nof workflow failure modes (session death, selector drift, latency cliffs,\npartial write-back). The driver must be credible *infrastructure*, not a demo.\n\n## Question\n\nWhat does a browser-level EMR sync transport need to be credible\ninfrastructure: how are credentialed sessions secured, which sandbox grounds\nthe work, and how do long-running browser workflows against EMR UIs actually\nfail?\n\n## Approach\n\nTwo gather waves on 2026-06-11 (see `state.yaml` for the plan). Wave one:\nprior vault context, the OpenEMR public demo page, OpenEMR Docker self-hosting\ndocs, and Anthropic's computer-use security/limitations documentation. Wave\ntwo (build-vs-adopt): framework evaluations of the Stagehand Python SDK,\nbrowser-use, Skyvern, and Playwright, plus cloud deployment options — each\nevaluated against the wave-one decisions rather than in the abstract. The\nfailure taxonomy below is a seed structure — its rows accrue from tracer-spike\nruns in the driver repository, each observed class feeding retry/idempotency/\nobservability design.\n\n## Findings\n\n### Security posture\n\nGrounded in the vendor's own guidance for computer-use agents\n[ai-found: raw/04]:\n\n1. **Synthetic data only.** The sandbox holds zero real patient data, ever.\n   This is scope, not mitigation — there is no failure mode in which PHI is\n   exposed because no PHI exists in the loop.\n2. **Container isolation, minimal privileges.** The driver and the browser it\n   controls run in a dedicated container/VM (\"dedicated virtual machine or\n   container with minimal privileges\" — raw/04). The Anthropic reference\n   implementation itself is Docker-contained.\n3. **Network allowlist.** The browser environment can reach the sandbox EMR\n   and nothing else (\"limiting internet access to an allowlist of domains\" —\n   raw/04). An injected instruction cannot exfiltrate to a host it cannot\n   resolve.\n4. **Credentials outside the model loop.** DOM-first automation performs\n   login programmatically (selectors + secret store), so credentials never\n   enter a prompt. The vendor path of last resort — credentials in prompt XML\n   tags — is documented to increase prompt-injection blast radius (raw/04);\n   the DOM-first default avoids it structurally.\n5. **Session/audit boundary.** Every driver action that mutates EMR state is\n   logged as an auditable event; write-back operations carry idempotency keys\n   so a replay after partial failure cannot double-apply. This is where the\n   driver meets HDP's audit/provenance primitives.\n6. **HITL gates on consequential writes.** Human confirmation before\n   meaningful real-world consequences (raw/04) aligns with HDP's existing\n   confidence-gated HITL design — the transport inherits the platform's\n   review checkpoint rather than inventing its own.\n7. **Prompt-injection stance.** Rendered EMR content is untrusted input.\n   Defense in depth: DOM-first control (the model is not steering from\n   screenshots in the default path), Anthropic's screenshot classifiers when\n   vision assist is active, allowlisted egress, and HITL gates — the docs are\n   explicit that precautions remain necessary even with the classifier layer\n   (raw/04).\n\n### Sandbox selection — self-hosted OpenEMR (decision)\n\n**Decision: self-hosted OpenEMR via the official Docker production compose,\nversion-pinned.** [ai-found: raw/02, raw/03]\n\n| Criterion | Public demo (`demo.openemr.io`) | Self-hosted Docker |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| State persistence | Wiped daily at 8:00 UTC | We control reset timing |\n| Isolation | Shared with other visitors | Single-tenant |\n| Authorization for automated traffic | No AUP stated either way | Our infrastructure |\n| Version stability | Tracks upstream | Pinned (e.g. `7.0.3`) |\n| Synthetic patients | Two portal patients guaranteed | Seeded deliberately |\n| Setup cost | Zero | `docker compose up`, ~5-10 min, arm64-capable |\n\nThe daily wipe alone disqualifies the public demo for failure-taxonomy work —\nmulti-day observation of session death and drift requires state we own. The\ndemo remains useful for quick manual UI recon. Gap to resolve at spike time:\ndefault ports/credentials and synthetic-data loading live in the Docker Hub\npage/compose files, not DOCKER_README.md (raw/03).\n\n### DOM-first, vision-assist (decision)\n\n**Decision: DOM-driven automation is the primary control loop; vision is\nassist and fallback.** The vendor's own limitation list argues for this\n[ai-found: raw/04]: latency \"too slow compared to regular human-directed\ncomputer actions,\" coordinate hallucination in vision-driven clicking,\nscrolling unreliability, and degraded reliability against niche applications\n— EMR UIs being exactly that. DOM selectors are deterministic, fast, cheap,\nand auditable (a selector either matched or it didn't; a logged action replay\nis exact). Vision assist earns its place where the DOM fails: canvas-rendered\nor legacy widgets, selector-drift recovery (visually re-locating a control\nwhose selector broke), and CAPTCHAs-class anomalies that should halt for human\nreview anyway.\n\n### Failure taxonomy (seed)\n\nClasses named in #18; rows accrue from spike runs in the driver repo. Each\nobserved failure gets: detection signal, blast radius, hardening\nrecommendation.\n\n| Class | What it looks like | Hardening direction (hypothesis) |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Session death | Auth timeout/logout mid-workflow | Checkpointed orchestration; re-auth + resume from last checkpoint |\n| Selector drift | EMR update changes DOM; selectors stop matching | Versioned selector maps; vision-assisted re-location; drift alarms |\n| Latency cliffs | Page loads stall; waits time out unpredictably | Adaptive timeouts; circuit breakers; observability on wait distributions |\n| Partial write-back | Multi-field form submit interrupted midway | Idempotency keys; read-after-write verification; transactional batching where the UI allows |\n\nThe infrastructure interest is in this column structure — retries,\nidempotent write-back, checkpointed orchestration, observability — more than\nin any single extraction's accuracy.\n\n### Build-vs-adopt: framework evaluation (decision, proposed)\n\n**Decision: build the driver on Playwright (deterministic loop) + DBOS\n(durable checkpoint/resume); evaluate Stagehand's BYOB pattern for the\nLLM-fallback layer during the spike; borrow browser-use's DOM serialization\nand Skyvern's failure semantics as reference architecture, not dependencies.**\n[ai-found: raw/05, raw/06, raw/07; durable execution raw/08]\n\nThe 2026 production consensus independently converged on the hub's wave-one\ncontrol-loop decision: deterministic DOM code primary, LLM engaged only where\nthe page is unpredictable. Evaluated against that decision:\n\n| Candidate | License | Verdict | Why |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Playwright (Python) | Apache-2.0 | **Adopt** — deterministic engine | Auto-waiting, storage_state login reuse, per-action traces, CDP reconnect (browser survives driver restart); no disqualifiers. Gap list (audit log, re-auth loop, step retry, egress enforcement) is the driver's actual product surface |\n| DBOS Transact | MIT | **Adopt** — checkpoint/resume layer | Embedded Python library, Postgres-backed (matches stack); crash-resume from last completed step; collapses workflow engine + queue + idempotency ledger into one component |\n| Stagehand Python SDK | MIT (SDK + server) | **Evaluate in spike** — fallback layer | BYOB maps exactly onto DOM-first/LLM-fallback (own Playwright page passes into `observe/act/extract`); fully self-hostable via embedded open-source server. Frictions: Node server sidecar, Python SDK lacks act-level caching/self-heal the TS original has |\n| browser-use | MIT (core) | **Reference / possible component** | Indexed-element DOM serializer is the best off-the-shelf page representation for drift recovery and is callable standalone; but pre-1.0 with two foundation swaps in 18 months, and its deterministic-replay sister project (workflow-use) is early-stage and AGPL |\n| Skyvern | AGPL-3.0 | **Reference architecture only** | LLM-per-step control loop inverts the ratified decision; AGPL bars a hard dependency in an MIT driver repo. Worth reading: stable-ID element tree + annotated-screenshot grounding, mutation-observer drift detection, workflow failure semantics (`continue_on_failure`, error-code mapping, human-pause blocks) |\n\nWhat remains in-house — and is the differentiating surface, not incidental\nglue: versioned selector maps, EMR workflow definitions, read-after-write\nverification, the structured PHI-minimal audit log, failure classification\n(one `TimeoutError` → dead-session vs latency vs drift), and the\n`hh-emr-sync` adapter contract. Notably, no evaluated framework ships durable\ncheckpoint/resume for long-running jobs — confirming the seam the wave-one\ncontract analysis identified.\n\n### Cloud deployment (decision, proposed)\n\n**Decision: spike runs local/single-VM (synthetic data — anywhere works);\nthe production-shaped reference topology is self-hosted workers on a\nBAA-covered cloud, with managed browser infrastructure recorded as a\ncredible alternative.** [ai-found: raw/08]\n\nSelf-hosted shape: container workers (ECS Fargate-class — no runtime limits,\n~2 GB per browser task) pulling jobs from the Postgres-backed queue;\ncheckpoint store and outbox in the same Postgres; secrets manager for EMR\ncredentials; VPC egress allowlist enforced at the network layer (the\nwave-one posture's structural control, in cloud terms); LLM-assist calls\nrouted through a BAA-covered model platform so even fallback screenshots\nstay inside one compliance boundary. One practical constraint shapes the\ntopology: EMR and payer portals frequently allowlist source IPs, so egress\nmust present a static IP (NAT/pinned proxy) — native to a VPC, awkward for\nrotating managed fleets.\n\nManaged alternative: Browserbase (the infrastructure behind Stagehand)\ndocuments SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA BAAs on request, a zero-data-retention mode,\nand per-session dedicated VMs — so the managed path is compliance-viable,\ntrading vendor dependency for isolation engineering not built in-house. The\nspike costs nothing to keep portable across both: the driver talks to a CDP\nendpoint either way.\n\n## Synthesis\n\nA credible browser-level EMR sync transport is **a hardened, audited,\nDOM-first driver running against owned, synthetic-only infrastructure** — not\na vision-loop agent pointed at a shared demo. The security posture is mostly\nstructural (isolation, allowlist, credentials outside the model loop,\nsynthetic-only scope) rather than behavioral, which is what makes it\ndefensible. The sandbox decision (self-hosted, pinned OpenEMR) follows from\nneeding multi-day failure state; the DOM-first decision follows from the\nvendor's own limitation list. What remains genuinely open — how these\nworkflows fail in practice — is empirical, and the taxonomy table is the\ninstrument for capturing it.\n\nAdapter-contract implications for the `hh-emr-sync` seam (#11): the contract\nmust accommodate idempotency keys, checkpoint/resume semantics, and\nasynchronous completion — an HTTP adapter satisfies these trivially; an\nautomation adapter requires them. If the seam bakes in synchronous\nrequest/response, the automation transport will not slot in.\n\nThe build-vs-adopt pass narrows what the driver repository actually is:\nfoundations are adoptable (Playwright for the deterministic loop, DBOS for\ndurability), so the repository's own code concentrates on the domain layer —\nselector maps, workflow definitions, audit, failure classification, and the\nadapter contract. That is the right shape for a tracer-bullet project: the\ncustom code is exactly the part with research value.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Driver repository: name and visibility (pending owner decision); hub links\n  out once created.\n- OpenEMR synthetic-patient seeding: best mechanism (built-in demo data vs\n  Synthea import) — resolve at spike time.\n- Default ports/credentials for the production compose — Docker Hub page.\n- Which OASIS-relevant OpenEMR workflows make the first tracer target (visit\n  documentation? assessment forms?).\n- Stagehand Python: does the agent-level cache entry have a server-side\n  replay-submission path, or is replay fully client-built? Conducted 2026-06-11 (main session, orchestrator). Research pre-fill:
`vault/research/computer-use-emr-sync/` (8 sources, 6 user-ratified
decisions) answers the approach/integration baseline; questions below cover
only the dimensions the research left open. Answers recorded verbatim from
AskUserQuestion selections.

## Dim 1 — Users & their workflows

**Q:** Who is the tracer-phase user, and through what surface?
**A (user):** "Both in tracer" — CLI + thin API.

Orchestrator interpretation (flagged for challenger review): CLI is the
primary developer/researcher surface (run job, resume job, inspect audit
log); the thin API is a FastAPI layer exposing the same job operations
(submit, status, resume) so the eventual `hh-emr-sync` adapter contract has
a real HTTP shape to integrate against. No UI. If "thin API" meant
something broader, this is a NEEDS CLARIFICATION.

## Dim 2 — Scope & functional requirements

**Q:** Driver repository name?
**A (user):** `emr-sync-driver` — standalone framing, no HDP coupling in
the name.

**Q:** Repository visibility from creation?
**A (user):** Public from creation. Synthetic-only, zero application
context; the tracer is the portfolio's runnable slice. Repo creation
itself remains a main-session user sign-off at execution time (irreversible
op per CLAUDE.md delegation rules).

**Q:** Is the LLM-fallback layer (Stagehand BYOB evaluation) part of the
tracer's first thread?
**A (user):** Gated phase after deterministic E2E — prove the deterministic
skeleton first; Stagehand evaluation becomes its own phase with its own
evidence. Matches ratified DOM-first-primary.

Non-goals (from research scope + dispatch context, unchallenged): no OASIS
data modeling in the tracer; no vision-primary implementation; no PHI ever
(synthetic only); driver implementation stays out of the HDP repo.

## Dim 3 — Integration & data flow

**Q:** Does the tracer consume HDP packages (hdp-audit, hdp-outbox —
currently empty shells), or stand alone?
**A (user):** Standalone, converge later — HDP packages are pre-trim empty
shells (#11 in flight); the adapter contract is the deliberate seam, and
the driver's audit/outbox interfaces inform HDP's primitives from real
usage.

Pre-filled from research (ratified): consumes self-hosted pinned OpenEMR
(docker-compose, synthetic patients); produces taxonomy rows + hardening
recommendations back to the hub (#18 exit conditions) and adapter-contract
implications to #11's emr-sync seam; foundations Playwright (deterministic
loop) + DBOS (Postgres-backed checkpoint/resume).

## Dim 4 — Quality criteria

**Q:** Done-bar for the deterministic tracer phase — confirm or adjust:
(1) E2E thread completes against self-hosted OpenEMR (login → navigate →
read field → write field → read-after-write verify); (2) kill -9 mid-job →
resume completes from last checkpoint without re-applying writes; (3) ≥3
taxonomy rows filled from observed failures, each with a hardening
recommendation; (4) audit log replays the full job action-by-action.
**A (user):** Confirm all four.

Quality bar (user-directed, this session): tracer-bullet quality — kept
code, production skeleton, NOT throwaway spike code. "No shortcuts.
Shortcuts lead to bad assumptions and refactors are costly downstream."

## Dim 5 — Risks & unknowns

**Q:** Constraints on where the tracer runs and how long it should take?
**A (user):** Local Mac (arm64), no deadline pressure — quality over speed.

Known unknowns carried from research (hub open questions):
- Stagehand Python agent-cache replay path (server-side or client-built) —
  measure during the gated fallback phase

# Phase 4 SYNTHESIZE — decision log
decisions:
  - section: Security posture
    proposed_by: ai
    revised_by: "user (ratified 2026-06-11, main session)"
    rationale: >
      Structural-over-behavioral framing: synthetic-only scope, isolation,
      allowlist, credentials outside the model loop — each eliminates a
      failure mode rather than mitigating it.
    rejected_alternatives:
      - alternative: "Credentials provided to the model in prompt XML tags (vendor path)"
        reason_rejected: "Docs themselves flag login-in-prompt as increased prompt-injection risk; DOM-first login avoids it structurally"
  - section: Sandbox selection
    proposed_by: ai
    revised_by: "user (ratified 2026-06-11, main session)"
    rationale: >
      Failure-taxonomy work needs multi-day owned state; public demo wipes
      daily, is shared, and has no AUP authorizing sustained automation.
    rejected_alternatives:
      - alternative: "Public demo.openemr.io instances as the spike sandbox"
        reason_rejected: "Daily 8:00 UTC wipe destroys taxonomy state; shared tenancy confounds observations; sustained automated traffic against community infra without an AUP is not defensible"
  - section: DOM-first, vision-assist
    proposed_by: ai
    revised_by: "user (ratified 2026-06-11, main session)"
    rationale: >
      Vendor limitation list (latency, coordinate hallucination, scroll
      unreliability, niche-app degradation) argues against vision as the
      primary loop; DOM selectors are deterministic and auditable.
    rejected_alternatives:
      - alternative: "Vision-primary control loop (screenshot-driven)"
        reason_rejected: "Slower, costlier, hallucination-prone per vendor docs; reserved for canvas/legacy widgets and selector-drift recovery"
  - section: Failure taxonomy (seed)
    proposed_by: ai
    revised_by: "user (ratified 2026-06-11, main session)"
    rationale: >
      Empirical rows cannot be pre-derived; the table fixes the column
      structure (detection, blast radius, hardening) so spike runs have a
      place to land observations.
    rejected_alternatives:
      - alternative: "Pre-populate taxonomy from web literature on flaky browser automation"
        reason_rejected: "#18 explicitly wants taxonomy accrued from spike runs; literature rows would be unverified filler"
  - section: "Build-vs-adopt: framework evaluation"
    proposed_by: ai
    revised_by: "user (ratified 2026-06-11, main session)"
    rationale: >
      Adopt foundations, own the domain layer: Playwright (Apache-2.0) for the
      deterministic loop, DBOS (MIT, Postgres-embedded) for checkpoint/resume;
      evaluate Stagehand BYOB for the LLM-fallback in the spike; browser-use
      DOM serializer and Skyvern failure semantics as reference architecture.
      No evaluated framework ships durable checkpoint/resume — the in-house
      seam is confirmed, and the custom code concentrates on the parts with
      research value (selector maps, audit, failure classification, adapter
      contract).
    rejected_alternatives:
      - alternative: "browser-use as the driver core"
        reason_rejected: "Agent-first default inverts DOM-first-primary; pre-1.0 with two foundation swaps in 18 months; its deterministic-replay sister project is early-stage and AGPL"
      - alternative: "Skyvern as a dependency"
        reason_rejected: "LLM-per-decision-step inverts the ratified control loop; AGPL bars hard dependency in an MIT driver repo; no deterministic replay"
      - alternative: "Temporal for durability"
        reason_rejected: "External cluster to operate; DBOS covers the need embedded in Postgres at this throughput — Temporal is the migrate-to-if-walls-hit path"
  - section: Cloud deployment
    proposed_by: ai
    revised_by: "user (ratified 2026-06-11, main session)"
    rationale: >
      Spike runs local/single-VM (synthetic data). Production-shaped reference
      topology: self-hosted container workers (Fargate-class) + Postgres
      (queue/checkpoint/outbox) + secrets manager + VPC egress allowlist +
      BAA-covered LLM platform — one compliance boundary. Managed browser
      infra (Browserbase: SOC 2 II, HIPAA BAA, zero-retention, per-session
      VMs) recorded as a viable alternative; portal source-IP allowlisting
      favors the static-egress VPC shape. Driver stays portable: it talks to
      a CDP endpoint either way.
    rejected_alternatives:
      - alternative: "Serverless functions (Lambda-class) for browser workers"
        reason_rejected: "15-minute runtime ceilings vs minutes-to-long jobs with checkpoint/resume; browser memory footprint and reconnect topology fit container workers"

# Computer-use as an EMR sync transport

Living hub for GitHub #18 (parent epic #14). Accrues alongside the driver
spike — a record, not a gating phase.

## Situation

Many EMR systems serving home health expose weak or no integration APIs.
`hh-emr-sync` today declares only `httpx` as its transport dependency,
presuming an API that many target systems lack (GH #14). OpenEMR is already
known to this vault as a schema-design reference [ai-found: raw/01]; here it
reappears in a different role — a real EMR UI to automate against.

## Complication

Browser-level automation (DOM-driven, vision-assisted) is a credible
additional transport for API-poor targets, but credentialed browser sessions
against a medical-records UI carry a threat model that HTTP clients do not:
prompt injection from rendered content, credential exposure, and a long tail
of workflow failure modes (session death, selector drift, latency cliffs,
partial write-back). The driver must be credible *infrastructure*, not a demo.

## Question

What does a browser-level EMR sync transport need to be credible
infrastructure: how are credentialed sessions secured, which sandbox grounds
the work, and how do long-running browser workflows against EMR UIs actually
fail?

## Approach

Two gather waves on 2026-06-11 (see `state.yaml` for the plan). Wave one:
prior vault context, the OpenEMR public demo page, OpenEMR Docker self-hosting
docs, and Anthropic's computer-use security/limitations documentation. Wave
two (build-vs-adopt): framework evaluations of the Stagehand Python SDK,
browser-use, Skyvern, and Playwright, plus cloud deployment options — each
evaluated against the wave-one decisions rather than in the abstract. The
failure taxonomy below is a seed structure — its rows accrue from tracer-spike
runs in the driver repository, each observed class feeding retry/idempotency/
observability design.

## Findings

### Security posture

Grounded in the vendor's own guidance for computer-use agents
[ai-found: raw/04]:

1. **Synthetic data only.** The sandbox holds zero real patient data, ever.
   This is scope, not mitigation — there is no failure mode in which PHI is
   exposed because no PHI exists in the loop.
2. **Container isolation, minimal privileges.** The driver and the browser it
   controls run in a dedicated container/VM ("dedicated virtual machine or
   container with minimal privileges" — raw/04). The Anthropic reference
   implementation itself is Docker-contained.
3. **Network allowlist.** The browser environment can reach the sandbox EMR
   and nothing else ("limiting internet access to an allowlist of domains" —
   raw/04). An injected instruction cannot exfiltrate to a host it cannot
   resolve.
4. **Credentials outside the model loop.** DOM-first automation performs
   login programmatically (selectors + secret store), so credentials never
   enter a prompt. The vendor path of last resort — credentials in prompt XML
   tags — is documented to increase prompt-injection blast radius (raw/04);
   the DOM-first default avoids it structurally.
5. **Session/audit boundary.** Every driver action that mutates EMR state is
   logged as an auditable event; write-back operations carry idempotency keys
   so a replay after partial failure cannot double-apply. This is where the
   driver meets HDP's audit/provenance primitives.
6. **HITL gates on consequential writes.** Human confirmation before
   meaningful real-world consequences (raw/04) aligns with HDP's existing
   confidence-gated HITL design — the transport inherits the platform's
   review checkpoint rather than inventing its own.
7. **Prompt-injection stance.** Rendered EMR content is untrusted input.
   Defense in depth: DOM-first control (the model is not steering from
   screenshots in the default path), Anthropic's screenshot classifiers when
   vision assist is active, allowlisted egress, and HITL gates — the docs are
   explicit that precautions remain necessary even with the classifier layer
   (raw/04).

### Sandbox selection — self-hosted OpenEMR (decision)

**Decision: self-hosted OpenEMR via the official Docker production compose,
version-pinned.** [ai-found: raw/02, raw/03]

| Criterion | Public demo (`demo.openemr.io`) | Self-hosted Docker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| State persistence | Wiped daily at 8:00 UTC | We control reset timing |
| Isolation | Shared with other visitors | Single-tenant |
| Authorization for automated traffic | No AUP stated either way | Our infrastructure |
| Version stability | Tracks upstream | Pinned (e.g. `7.0.3`) |
| Synthetic patients | Two portal patients guaranteed | Seeded deliberately |
| Setup cost | Zero | `docker compose up`, ~5-10 min, arm64-capable |

The daily wipe alone disqualifies the public demo for failure-taxonomy work —
multi-day observation of session death and drift requires state we own. The
demo remains useful for quick manual UI recon. Gap to resolve at spike time:
default ports/credentials and synthetic-data loading live in the Docker Hub
page/compose files, not DOCKER_README.md (raw/03).

### DOM-first, vision-assist (decision)

**Decision: DOM-driven automation is the primary control loop; vision is
assist and fallback.** The vendor's own limitation list argues for this
[ai-found: raw/04]: latency "too slow compared to regular human-directed
computer actions," coordinate hallucination in vision-driven clicking,
scrolling unreliability, and degraded reliability against niche applications
— EMR UIs being exactly that. DOM selectors are deterministic, fast, cheap,
and auditable (a selector either matched or it didn't; a logged action replay
is exact). Vision assist earns its place where the DOM fails: canvas-rendered
or legacy widgets, selector-drift recovery (visually re-locating a control
whose selector broke), and CAPTCHAs-class anomalies that should halt for human
review anyway.

### Failure taxonomy (seed)

Classes named in #18; rows accrue from spike runs in the driver repo. Each
observed failure gets: detection signal, blast radius, hardening
recommendation.

| Class | What it looks like | Hardening direction (hypothesis) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Session death | Auth timeout/logout mid-workflow | Checkpointed orchestration; re-auth + resume from last checkpoint |
| Selector drift | EMR update changes DOM; selectors stop matching | Versioned selector maps; vision-assisted re-location; drift alarms |
| Latency cliffs | Page loads stall; waits time out unpredictably | Adaptive timeouts; circuit breakers; observability on wait distributions |
| Partial write-back | Multi-field form submit interrupted midway | Idempotency keys; read-after-write verification; transactional batching where the UI allows |

The infrastructure interest is in this column structure — retries,
idempotent write-back, checkpointed orchestration, observability — more than
in any single extraction's accuracy.

### Build-vs-adopt: framework evaluation (decision, proposed)

**Decision: build the driver on Playwright (deterministic loop) + DBOS
(durable checkpoint/resume); evaluate Stagehand's BYOB pattern for the
LLM-fallback layer during the spike; borrow browser-use's DOM serialization
and Skyvern's failure semantics as reference architecture, not dependencies.**
[ai-found: raw/05, raw/06, raw/07; durable execution raw/08]

The 2026 production consensus independently converged on the hub's wave-one
control-loop decision: deterministic DOM code primary, LLM engaged only where
the page is unpredictable. Evaluated against that decision:

| Candidate | License | Verdict | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Playwright (Python) | Apache-2.0 | **Adopt** — deterministic engine | Auto-waiting, storage_state login reuse, per-action traces, CDP reconnect (browser survives driver restart); no disqualifiers. Gap list (audit log, re-auth loop, step retry, egress enforcement) is the driver's actual product surface |
| DBOS Transact | MIT | **Adopt** — checkpoint/resume layer | Embedded Python library, Postgres-backed (matches stack); crash-resume from last completed step; collapses workflow engine + queue + idempotency ledger into one component |
| Stagehand Python SDK | MIT (SDK + server) | **Evaluate in spike** — fallback layer | BYOB maps exactly onto DOM-first/LLM-fallback (own Playwright page passes into `observe/act/extract`); fully self-hostable via embedded open-source server. Frictions: Node server sidecar, Python SDK lacks act-level caching/self-heal the TS original has |
| browser-use | MIT (core) | **Reference / possible component** | Indexed-element DOM serializer is the best off-the-shelf page representation for drift recovery and is callable standalone; but pre-1.0 with two foundation swaps in 18 months, and its deterministic-replay sister project (workflow-use) is early-stage and AGPL |
| Skyvern | AGPL-3.0 | **Reference architecture only** | LLM-per-step control loop inverts the ratified decision; AGPL bars a hard dependency in an MIT driver repo. Worth reading: stable-ID element tree + annotated-screenshot grounding, mutation-observer drift detection, workflow failure semantics (`continue_on_failure`, error-code mapping, human-pause blocks) |

What remains in-house — and is the differentiating surface, not incidental
glue: versioned selector maps, EMR workflow definitions, read-after-write
verification, the structured PHI-minimal audit log, failure classification
(one `TimeoutError` → dead-session vs latency vs drift), and the
`hh-emr-sync` adapter contract. Notably, no evaluated framework ships durable
checkpoint/resume for long-running jobs — confirming the seam the wave-one
contract analysis identified.

### Cloud deployment (decision, proposed)

**Decision: spike runs local/single-VM (synthetic data — anywhere works);
the production-shaped reference topology is self-hosted workers on a
BAA-covered cloud, with managed browser infrastructure recorded as a
credible alternative.** [ai-found: raw/08]

Self-hosted shape: container workers (ECS Fargate-class — no runtime limits,
~2 GB per browser task) pulling jobs from the Postgres-backed queue;
checkpoint store and outbox in the same Postgres; secrets manager for EMR
credentials; VPC egress allowlist enforced at the network layer (the
wave-one posture's structural control, in cloud terms); LLM-assist calls
routed through a BAA-covered model platform so even fallback screenshots
stay inside one compliance boundary. One practical constraint shapes the
topology: EMR and payer portals frequently allowlist source IPs, so egress
must present a static IP (NAT/pinned proxy) — native to a VPC, awkward for
rotating managed fleets.

Managed alternative: Browserbase (the infrastructure behind Stagehand)
documents SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA BAAs on request, a zero-data-retention mode,
and per-session dedicated VMs — so the managed path is compliance-viable,
trading vendor dependency for isolation engineering not built in-house. The
spike costs nothing to keep portable across both: the driver talks to a CDP
endpoint either way.

## Synthesis

A credible browser-level EMR sync transport is **a hardened, audited,
DOM-first driver running against owned, synthetic-only infrastructure** — not
a vision-loop agent pointed at a shared demo. The security posture is mostly
structural (isolation, allowlist, credentials outside the model loop,
synthetic-only scope) rather than behavioral, which is what makes it
defensible. The sandbox decision (self-hosted, pinned OpenEMR) follows from
needing multi-day failure state; the DOM-first decision follows from the
vendor's own limitation list. What remains genuinely open — how these
workflows fail in practice — is empirical, and the taxonomy table is the
instrument for capturing it.

Adapter-contract implications for the `hh-emr-sync` seam (#11): the contract
must accommodate idempotency keys, checkpoint/resume semantics, and
asynchronous completion — an HTTP adapter satisfies these trivially; an
automation adapter requires them. If the seam bakes in synchronous
request/response, the automation transport will not slot in.

The build-vs-adopt pass narrows what the driver repository actually is:
foundations are adoptable (Playwright for the deterministic loop, DBOS for
durability), so the repository's own code concentrates on the domain layer —
selector maps, workflow definitions, audit, failure classification, and the
adapter contract. That is the right shape for a tracer-bullet project: the
custom code is exactly the part with research value.

## Open questions

- Driver repository: name and visibility (pending owner decision); hub links
  out once created.
- OpenEMR synthetic-patient seeding: best mechanism (built-in demo data vs
  Synthea import) — resolve at spike time.
- Default ports/credentials for the production compose — Docker Hub page.
- Which OASIS-relevant OpenEMR workflows make the first tracer target (visit
  documentation? assessment forms?).
- Stagehand Python: does the agent-level cache entry have a server-side
  replay-submission path, or is replay fully client-built? (raw/05 flags
  UNVERIFIED) — measure during the spike's fallback evaluation.

## Next actions

- Create the driver repository (Playwright + DBOS scaffold per the
  build-vs-adopt decision); first tracer run against self-hosted OpenEMR.
- Begin populating taxonomy rows from observed failures (one hardening

- Feed adapter-contract implications into the #11 trim spec's emr-sync seam.
